title: The question in dispute: can the precepts be kept without special grace so that the act is morally good?
source_text: IX. Verum inter eos quaeritur An absque speciali gratia, & solo generalis auxilii beneficio, sic possint praecepta divina servari, ut quamvis istud ex charitate non fiat, nec sit aeternae vitae meritorium, in eo tamen peccatum vitetur, & actio sit bona & honesta moraliter? Super qua re variae sunt & discrepantes eorum sententiae.
pass_a_gloss: IX. But among them it is asked Whether without special grace, and by the benefit of the general help alone, the divine precepts can so be kept that, although it is not done from charity, nor is meritorious of eternal life, yet in it sin is avoided, and the action is good and honest morally? On which matter their opinions are various and discordant.
pass_b_english: The question among them is this: can God's precepts be kept without special grace, by the general help alone, in such a way that, although the act is not done out of charity and does not merit eternal life, sin is still avoided and the act is morally good and honourable? On this their opinions differ widely.

lemmas.gloss: by the benefit of the general help alone
nor is meritorious of eternal life
their opinions are various and discordant

choices.why: God's ordinary cooperation with every created cause, as opposed to special grace; kept as the technical term.
